tool_input.command:
git add internal/doctor/procgroup_unix.go internal/doctor/procgroup_windows.go internal/doctor/procgroup_unix_test.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix(doctor): #10/#4 — precise unix/!unix build constraint, corrected process-group cleanup comment

Leader ruling on PR #515's remaining findings:

#10: procgroup_unix.go's `!windows` constraint claimed every non-Windows
target, including several (plan9, js/wasm) that lack the Unix
process-group APIs it uses. Narrowed to the precise `unix` constraint
(Go 1.19+); procgroup_windows.go widened to `!unix` as its fallback.
qodo's stated reason (this branch breaks those builds) was not
reproducible — internal/process already excludes them at the
merge-base, independent of this branch — but the constraint was
genuinely imprecise regardless, and the correct spelling costs
nothing. All four shipped targets (darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64,
linux/arm64, windows/amd64) still build clean.

#4: the escape qodo found is real — a hook child that calls setsid
before backgrounding leaves the process group entirely, so
kill(-pgid) cannot reach it. The actual defect was
setNewProcessGroup's doc comment claiming to kill "the whole tree a
sandboxed hook spawns," which overclaims exactly the way this
cluster's other fixes exist to correct. Narrowed the comment to what
kill(-pgid) actually delivers, named the setsid residual explicitly,
and noted that lifetime containment was never the sandbox's security
boundary — hook execution is untrusted-code execution by design
(DES-077's base ADR already documents no seccomp/chroot/network
isolation). No portable, unprivileged fix exists across every shipped
target; closing the escape itself is a platform-containment design
decision left to a scoped follow-up, not this round.
EOF
)"
